datasets.name: GBA Final Wards Delimitation 2025 (369 wards, with population)
datasets.licence: Other (Public Domain) as stated by the OpenCity portal
datasets.powers: Module 1 jurisdiction, Module 21 ward analytics, Module 22 map; spatial-block CV groups for every Bengaluru model
datasets.why_it_matters: The whole platform keys off which of the 369 wards a point falls in. Without it nothing else resolves.

datasets.name: Greater Chennai Corporation ward and zone boundaries (2022)
datasets.licence: As published by the OpenCity urban data portal
datasets.powers: Module 1 jurisdiction for Chennai, ward analytics, map, Tamil ward names
datasets.why_it_matters: GCC publishes ward numbers only. Place names here are DERIVED from OpenStreetMap, not official.
datasets.caveats: Ward names are not published in this source — wards are identified by number only | Zone assignment is derived by spatial join, not read from the ward source file | Ward map vintage is 2022; re-check for later delimitation

datasets.name: District and taluk boundaries — bengaluru
datasets.publisher: Local Government Directory (LGD) and Survey of India, via the india-geodata community compilation
datasets.powers: District and taluk for any point in Bengaluru
datasets.why_it_matters: Took taluk coverage from 3 taluks (revenue sheets only) to 100% of localities.
datasets.caveats: REPUBLISHED, NOT OFFICIAL. LGD and Survey of India are the upstream authorities; this project retrieved a community compilation of them, so it is T3 and reported as INDICATIVE. | VINTAGE IS NOT STATED per feature. Karnataka and Tamil Nadu have both reorganised taluks in recent years, so a name here may predate a reorganisation. | THIS LAYER CANNOT PRODUCE A SURVEY NUMBER. It answers which taluk a point falls in. Survey number remains sourced from the revenue sheets and stays UNAVAILABLE outside their footprint. | Hobli is not an LGD level and is not present in this layer. It remains available only where a revenue sheet covers the point.

datasets.name: Bengaluru Urban revenue maps — taluk, hobli, village, survey number
datasets.licence: As published by the OpenCity urban data portal
datasets.powers: Hobli, village and survey number (Module 1, Module 2)
datasets.why_it_matters: The only source of a survey number in the project, and it covers 7% of localities. Everything outside it returns UNAVAILABLE.
datasets.caveats: COVERAGE IS PARTIAL — only the taluks and hoblis published in this dataset are present. Points outside them return UNAVAILABLE. | A survey number from a digitised revenue sheet is INDICATIVE. It is not a legal determination of boundary or title; those are settled by the Sub-Registrar and a licensed surveyor. | Sheet vintage is not stated per file; treat as historical and re-verify before relying on it.

datasets.name: Reported flooding locations, Bengaluru Urban
datasets.licence: Other (Public Domain) as stated by the OpenCity portal
datasets.why_it_matters: Reported locations only. Explicitly NOT folded into the risk score, which still lists flood as excluded.
datasets.caveats: These are reported flooding locations, not a hazard model. No return period, depth, drainage capacity or terrain analysis is attached. Distance to the nearest reported point is NOT a flood risk score. | No reported point nearby does NOT mean the property does not flood. It means none was recorded in this dataset. | POINT DATA, NOT INUNDATION GEOMETRY. A point marks a reported location, not the extent of flooding around it. | No date is attached per point, so the reporting period is unknown and conditions may have changed since. | This layer does NOT feed the environmental risk score. Flood remains listed as excluded there (audit R7).

datasets.name: Bengaluru road width map — road centrelines with existing and proposed width
datasets.licence: Other (Public Domain) as stated by the OpenCity portal
datasets.powers: Module 8 road intelligence; offers a road width to Module 6 feasibility
datasets.why_it_matters: Contains TWO width columns. The proposed one would double reported buildable area city-wide if used.
datasets.caveats: NEITHER FIELD IS A SURVEYED ROAD WIDTH. Statutory FAR, height and setback depend on the width of the road abutting a specific plot, measured on the ground or taken from a sanctioned plan. | RR_WIDTH_P MUST NOT BE USED FOR FEASIBILITY. If it is a proposed width, using it would report floor area that is not permissible today — median proposed width is roughly double median existing. | COVERAGE IS BBMP-ERA — the former ~198-ward BBMP area, not all 369 Greater Bengaluru wards. Points outside it return UNAVAILABLE. | NO ROAD NAMES are published in this dataset, so a segment cannot be identified by name. | THIS IS NOT THE COMPLETE STREET NETWORK. It is a width map for the roads BBMP tracks — arterial and collector roads. Most residential lanes have no segment here. See coverage.measured below. | The road-hierarchy codes (MA, MI, PU, OR, IR, CR, PR) are published without a data dictionary. Expansions shown anywhere in this project are labelled unverified.

datasets.name: OpenStreetMap amenities, transport and government offices
datasets.powers: Modules 9, 10, 11 proximity; 11 GIS features in every model
datasets.why_it_matters: Adding these raised Bengaluru's honest spatial-CV R² from 0.3078 to 0.4231.
datasets.caveats: OSM completeness varies across Greater Bengaluru; absence of a facility in this layer is not evidence that none exists | Government/private classification relies on OSM tagging and is unreliable; it is not an official directory | Jurisdiction is NOT determined by proximity — the nearest office is not necessarily the office with jurisdiction

datasets.name: OpenStreetMap locality gazetteer — bengaluru
datasets.powers: Locality search, geocoding the property dataset to wards
datasets.why_it_matters: Joins the T4 property dataset to real geography, which is what makes spatial-block CV possible.
datasets.caveats: Locality-level resolution only — a locality centroid is not the property's location | Matching a dataset locality string to an OSM place name is derived evidence, not proof of location

datasets.name: OpenStreetMap locality gazetteer — chennai (overpass)

datasets.why_it_matters: Supplies the Tamil ward names — 129 of 200; the rest are left blank rather than transliterated.
datasets.caveats: Locality-level resolution only — a locality centroid is not the property's location | Matching a dataset locality string to a place name is derived evidence, not proof of location

datasets.name: Bengaluru house price data — asking prices from listings
datasets.powers: Module 14 price prediction, 16 demand, 17-18 builder ROI, 19 buyer, 20 investor, quantile negotiation band
datasets.why_it_matters: ASKING prices, not transactions. Every price the platform predicts inherits that upward bias.
datasets.caveats: UPSTREAM ATTRIBUTION IS RECORDED, LICENCE IS NOT. The Kaggle dataset page is JavaScript-rendered and could not be read programmatically, so the licence is recorded as UNVERIFIED rather than guessed. Confirm it on the dataset page before any redistribution or commercial use. | RETRIEVED FROM A MIRROR, so the mirror's fidelity to the Kaggle original has not been byte-verified. The column set matches the well-known dataset, which is evidence, not proof. | NOT A GOVERNMENT REGISTER. These are ASKING prices scraped from listings, carrying a systematic upward bias of unknown size against transaction prices. | VINTAGE IS UNSTATED. Neither the mirror nor the notebook establishes when these listings were collected, which is why model confidence is capped at 0.45 regardless of validation score.

datasets.name: Chennai housing sales price — recorded sale prices
datasets.powers: Same modules for Chennai, plus Module 15 future price
datasets.why_it_matters: RECORDED SALE prices — the only real transaction data in the project. Period ends ~2015, and only 7 localities, so spatial CV has 7 blocks.
datasets.caveats: UPSTREAM ATTRIBUTION IS INFERRED, NOT CONFIRMED. The mirror's columns (SALES_PRICE, INT_SQFT, N_BEDROOM, DATE_SALE, AREA) match the well-known Kaggle dataset named above, but the mirror does not cite its own source and the Kaggle page could not be read programmatically. Treat the upstream link as the most likely origin, not an established one. | LICENCE UNVERIFIED for the same reason. | These ARE recorded sale prices including registration fee and commission — genuinely closer to transaction value than the Bengaluru asking-price data. | PERIOD ENDS AROUND 2015. The absolute levels describe a historical market and must not be read as current values. | ONLY 7 LOCALITIES, so spatial validation has 7 blocks. Every model trained on it carries a low-block warning.

not_available.why: Per-property lookup behind SAS ID + mobile OTP with owner consent. No bulk feed, no query API. Automated retrieval would be both technically hostile and legally questionable.
Account required, one property at a time, and only to a party with a legitimate interest.
No public API and terms do not permit automated retrieval. The platform links to it and stores what a person records by hand.
Karnataka does not publish transaction-level registration data at all. This is why the Bengaluru model trains on asking prices.
Mobile/web GIS app, no public API. Its boundaries are notional with 3-10 m GPS error and are not legally valid for disputes.
Published as planning-district PDF map sheets. No machine-readable polygon layer exists, so Module 5 cannot be geographic.
Audit task R5, closed as a negative: PDF jurisdiction maps for 12 local planning authorities, no shapefile or KML anywhere.
Audit task R1, still open. The host presents an incomplete TLS certificate chain and could not be reached by two independent clients. Not worked around.
The published field sums to ~6x the real total and 125 of 369 rows fail male+female=total. No figure is published.
